faq.q: Is Lake City a residential neighbourhood?
faq.a: No. Lake City is an industrial and business-centre district in north-east Burnaby; the Lake City Community Plan (adopted 2000) designates it as a mixed-use area for commercial/office and industrial/business centre uses, and there are few or no homes in it.

faq.q: Why are there no Lake City sales numbers in this file?
faq.a: Because SnapStats publishes no Lake City sub-area row for Burnaby in its September 2026 report — there is no sub-area inventory, solds or sales ratio to report. The Burnaby figures in Section 2 are community-level context only, not Lake City figures (as of September 2026, Source: SnapStats GVR September 2026 report).

faq.q: What kinds of businesses belong in Lake City?
faq.a: The City's employment-lands policy defines industrial lands for distribution, warehousing, repair, construction yards, wholesale, manufacturing, trade and e-commerce, and the Lake City plan adds commercial/office and business-centre frameworks — confirm a specific use against the parcel's current zoning district in writing.

faq.q: Which plan governs Lake City today?
faq.a: The Burnaby 2050 Official Community Plan (adopted December 9, 2025) sets the framework and takes precedence over older community-plan maps; the Lake City Community Plan (2000) remains the district's adopted policy guideline underneath it.
